subject.title: [Bug]:  Session status blind spot | Sessions in done state excluded from context saturation monitoring — agents run dead for hours undetected

question: Should OpenClaw add a native context-pressure alert/recovery contract for saturated terminal `done` sessions, and where should that alert surface?
rationale: Source inspection shows the gap, but the fix changes diagnostics and recovery semantics; automation should not choose the threshold, notification target, or cleanup behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add Terminal Context-Pressure Alert
options.body: Create a diagnostics/session-health contract that alerts on saturated terminal rows and leaves recovery action explicit and observable.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Session Health
options.body: Defer this issue into a broader session/zombie/heartbeat health design that also covers parent notification and idle runaway cases.

options.title: Keep Status-Only Visibility
options.body: Decline a native alert for now and rely on `status`/`sessions.list` context usage plus external operator monitoring.

recommendation.title: Add Terminal Context-Pressure Alert
recommendation.body: Create a diagnostics/session-health contract that alerts on saturated terminal rows and leaves recovery action explicit and observable.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest inspected history on diagnostic attention and status surfaces where the product contract would likely land.
